_comment: MultiHitBoxLib hitbox profile for orespawn:the_queen.
All ten parts are listed in synched-bones, which means MHLib's
GeckolibBoneInformationCollectorLayer (auto-attached to QueenRenderer
via MixinGeoEntityRenderer) reads the bone's world position via
GeoBone#getWorldPosition each render frame, packs it into a
CPacketBoneInformation, and ships it server-ward. The server's
alignSynchedSubParts() then snaps each MHLibPartEntity to that
world position the next aiStep tick.
Bone names match danger.orespawn.entity.client.ModelTheQueen.geo.json
verbatim (legacy 1.7.10 'L'-prefixed naming retained from the original
model). The three heads are LHead / LHead4 / LHead12 -- distinct deep
chains, not duplicates of one bone. In the geo LHead is the +x head,
LHead4 the -x head and LHead12 the centre head (pivots x = 28 / -28 / 2).
Damage modifiers per directive:
heads = 1.0  (precision aiming reward),
body / legs = 0.5  (armoured),
wings / tail = 0.25  (glancing).
main-hitbox.canReceiveDamage = false forces ALL incoming damage to
route through a part (so the parent's giant 22x24 AABB -- orig
TheQueen.java:79 envelope, BOSS-007 -- cannot be trivially
face-tanked from below).
ENT-S-092 (2026-09-03, owner ruling): the renderer draws the Queen at the
1.7.10 scale 2.0 again (0.5 while PlayNicely), applied AFTER GeckoLib's
entityRenderTranslations capture, so every synced bone position MHLib
receives is the drawn one. Part sizes and pivots below are fitted per
part to the drawn geometry at 2.0 (rest pose), from GeckoLib 4.8.4's own
bake and matrix chain (src/g1tool QueenPartPlacementProbe), NOT a blanket
2x. Frame: the MHLib world frame at yaw 0, blocks, entity at the origin:
world +x = geo +x (GeckoLib's bake negates x, applyRotations' 180-degree
turn negates it back) and world +z = geo -z (heads at +z, tail at -z);
the collector ships the body yaw with every bone rotation, so the
pivots follow the bones at any yaw (MHLibPartEntity.applyInformation).
size = [max(x extent, z extent), y extent] of the drawn segment (the
bone's subtree minus the subtrees of its synced descendants,
so the three tail parts split the tail instead of nesting);
the aabb type has a square footprint, so the larger horizontal
extent is the width. Rounded to 0.01 block.
pivot = (bone world position - segment box bottom-centre) taken back
through MHLib's own pivot rotation (MHLibPartEntity.applyInformation
:424-434 rotates the pivot by the collector's summed bone rotation
before subtracting it), so the box sits ON the drawn segment at
rest instead of extending upward from the bone (old pivots were
all [0,0,0]). Where the bone sits centred in its segment this
reduces to pivot y = h/2 (Body1).
position = the bone's world position at 2.0, the fallback offset
alignSynchedSubParts uses before the first bone packet.
PlayNicely: TheQueen.mhlibGetEntitySizeScale = 0.25 scales sizes,
pivots and fallbacks (main box 5.5x6), matching the 0.5 draw.
Per part (old -> new; factor = new size / old size):
The square footprint over-covers the long axis of the elongated segments
(heads 12.6 long x 3.8 wide, wing 44.9 span x 20.7 chord, tail segments,
legs 12.8 fore-aft x 4.8 wide); an orientable box type would fit tighter.
